name: Veterans March

stars.name: March Major
stars.notes: Ancient, stable orange dwarf hosting all eight planets; the mustering light of the Assembly.

stars.name: March Minor
stars.notes: Dim red companion on a wide orbit; it hosts no planets, its domain swept clean by ancient close encounters.

stars.name: The Drumbeat
stars.notes: Stellar-mass black hole drifting ~900 AU out, invisible but for its lensing; the Assembly uses its gravity as a telescope.

planets.name: Kiln
planets.notes: Molten cinder used for high-temperature alloy smelting aboard orbital crucibles.

planets.name: Standardbear
planets.notes: Arid training world where demobilized regiments keep their edge running live-fire exercises.

planets.name: Hearthmark
planets.notes: Homeworld of the Grand Veteran Assembly: garrison towns, parade grounds, and the largest population of retired spacers anywhere.

planets.name: Saltpeter
planets.notes: Mining colony extracting nitrates and propellant feedstocks for the Assembly's munitions works.

planets.name: Warhorse
planets.notes: Fleet anchorage among its moons: decommissioned dreadnoughts moored in silent rows, ready for reactivation.

planets.name: Grey Picket
planets.notes: Sensor picket world whose arrays watch the approaches the Drumbeat does not cover.

planets.name: Last Muster
planets.notes: Veterans' cemetery world; every soldier who served the Assembly may lie here, and most choose to.

planets.name: Cold Beacon
planets.notes: Outer comm relay linking the muster yards to Assembly fleets across three sectors.

anomalies.name: The Counting Lens
anomalies.location: far outer system, near The Drumbeat
anomalies.notes: The black hole's lensing is deliberately exploited as a natural spyglass, letting Assembly observers read ship movements in neighboring sectors from home.

asteroid_belts.name: Drumline Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Ice mining feeds the fleet's water and propellant needs; veteran cooperatives hold every claim.

stations.name: Assembly Ring
stations.notes: Grand mustering yard where retired hulls are reactivated and new battle groups form under Assembly colors.

stations.name: Hearthmark High Port
stations.notes: Civilian-military trade port; pension offices, recruitment halls, and the sector's busiest crew hiring market.

stations.name: Listening Post Nine
stations.notes: Staffed observatory riding the lensing sweet spot; its officers see everything first and tell almost no one.

faction_control.notes: Sovereign polity of retired soldiers and their descendants; neutral by charter, formidable by reputation, and courted by every faction in a crisis.

history: Founded after the Frontier Wars when six demobilized fleets refused disbandment and instead bought the rights to this quiet orange-dwarf system.
Survived an attempted coup by a warlord admiral; the mutineers' flagship still hangs in Warhorse's orbit as a warning, stripped and dark.
Today the March is where anyone who needs a fleet comes to hire or borrow one — and the Assembly decides, slowly and by vote, who is worth arming.
description: An ancient orange sun warms eight hard-used worlds while, far beyond them, the invisible Drumbeat bends starlight like a lens. The system reads like a soldier's life: training grounds, a homeworld, mines, an anchorage, and a cemetery at the edge of the light.

Veterans March is the great muster point of the verge. The Assembly Ring reactivates old dreadnoughts by the dozen, Hearthmark's ports hum with crews seeking contracts, and traffic never drops below major-hub levels. Every faction maintains a liaison here; none maintains a base, because the Assembly forbids it and means it.

Opportunities abound for those the veterans trust, and so do questions. Listening Post Nine has begun reporting fleet movements nobody can account for, the Counting Lens recently imaged something at the galaxy's edge that was immediately classified, and the moored flagship at Warhorse is said to receive visitors after midnight. The Assembly votes on war slowly — but it is always counting.
